Default experience: The game includes a built-in relay service (enabled by default, no setup required). Players can launch and play immediately. All AI requests are routed through the developer's own server, which applies keyword filtering and progressive moderation on both input and output before forwarding to the AI model. Every player receives a free daily quota.
Monetization: One-time DLC purchases are available through Steam for additional turns beyond the free daily quota. These are single purchases, not subscriptions, priced $1–$10. DLC revenue covers the developer's costs.
Content guardrails: In Relay Mode, all requests pass through server-side multi-layer moderation — keyword filtering (red-line terms blocked immediately; yellow-line terms accumulate toward escalation), bidirectional input/output checks, and progressive restrictions for repeat violations.

To give a clearer picture: the game includes over 3,000 hand-crafted sprite frames, composed from thousands of hand-drawn body parts. I understand that some people may have concerns about the use of AI in the creative process. EQUILIBRIUM uses generative AI to power its core gameplay mechanic: the Policy Terminal.
LIVE-GENERATED CONTENT
When a player types a directive or law in natural language (e.g., "Abolish the luxury car tax"), the AI Engine analyzes the request in real time and generates a structured governmental dossier, including:
- Legislative feasibility analysis
- Budget impact and financial coverage
- Macroeconomic effects (GDP, debt, inflation)
- Social and political consensus projections
- Parliamentary vote simulation
Model used: Anthropic Claude, accessed via API.
Guardrails: AI output is constrained to a fixed set of structured fields defined by the developer. All numeric effects are clamped within bounds enforced by the simulation engine, so no AI output can produce values outside the game's defined ranges. The model operates only on the simulation state provided to it and cannot invent game data: commands that cannot be mapped to a valid government action are refused, and the player is offered bounded policy alternatives instead. No image, audio, or user-data generation is involved, and no player data is used to train any model.
Because responses are generated at runtime, outputs vary between playthroughs: the same directive may produce different wording and different outcomes.

We're just a small team who loves making games and we love using AI to make them even better.

This game uses generative AI in two ways.
During play: the character's replies are written by a language model and spoken by a speech model, and she can compose a short song when you ask for one. All of these models run on your own PC. The game does not connect to any outside AI service, and nothing you type or say is uploaded. Voices are synthetic; you can also create a voice from a recording you supply, which stays on your PC.
Made ahead of time: a library of body gestures the character uses while talking, the loading-screen illustration and some store artwork were made with generative models and reviewed by the developer. On the store page, the main trailer and the clips and images marked "AI-enhanced" are in-game footage re-rendered by video and image models to look more lifelike; some hairstyles and outfits in them are concept looks for future updates. Clips marked "In-game capture" and the trailer titled "Gameplay Trailer" are unprocessed. The trailers use AI-generated music.
Replies are generated live, so they can be wrong or out of character. You can report inappropriate AI output through the Steam Overlay.
Used in simple artwork, NPC chat systems, tactical realism systems, enhanced system design, economy management, debugging and design assistance.

The developer used generative AI tools during development to help create some art assets (such as character portraits, sprites, and background art) and marketing materials (store capsules and trailers), and to assist with text localization. All AI-assisted content was reviewed and edited by the developer. The game itself does not generate any content in real time and does not connect to AI services during gameplay.

Artificial intelligence was used to create the game. With the help of ChatGPT, we were able to analyze and organize several thousand messages from eco-volunteer chat groups, as well as dozens of media articles, podcasts, and vlogs about the spill. All of this was necessary to identify key events, troubling themes, and the moods of people involved in disaster response, and was used by a human author to further develop the plot and dialogue. The images were created using Midjourney. Photos of real landscapes, but not people, were used to generate prompts. The game’s music was generated in Stability AI. The code to adapt the existing game structure to the Ren’py framework was written using Cursor AI.

In this game, conversations with NPCs are powered by generative AI.
You can freely ask questions to villagers, and their responses are dynamically generated by AI on the spot.
Each character’s personality and background knowledge of the mystery are taken into account, allowing for natural dialogue and unique testimonies.
All AI-generated responses are carefully restricted to stay consistent with the game’s world and narrative, ensuring the mystery remains coherent and immersive.
Talking to AI characters is a key part of solving the case — gather clues, uncover keywords, and enjoy the thrill of free-form deduction as you get closer to the truth.

Most of our generated content has been carefully designed and built in advance, mainly related to cat travel and scenic spot replies. Local model generated content will align with Steam rules, and there will be no negative guidance in the generated content. We will strictly follow the rules and guidelines of the Steam platform to ensure that every output meets Steam's standards and requirements.
Generative AI was used to create some 2D background images during development. No AI-generated content is produced during gameplay.

Our game is about shooting movies. We also allow players to create their own movies, including having characters say the lines of the movie script. Players can write dialogue and generate audio. The 3D animated characters act out the script.

CielChan uses generative AI to create real-time conversation responses and voice synthesis. By default, a local AI model generates text responses, and bundled TTS engines convert those responses to speech directly on your device.
All core functionality is fully available offline, and no internet connection is required to use the application.
Optional cloud-based AI and voice features are available for advanced users. When enabled, these features may send text or audio data to selected third-party providers using user-provided API keys.
The AI model, voice synthesis, and core systems are included in the download, allowing CielChan to function independently offline.

Signal Ghost uses a bundled local language model to generate fictional character dialogue during play. It responds to player-written IRC and direct messages using character context, relationship history, and current mission state. Signal Ghost runs on the player's device; its chat does not require an external AI service. Some pre-generated artwork was created with generative AI and edited for use in the game.

When user chat while playing a game, users will be communicating with the LLM model and make a voice Azure TTS.
The Character appearance is an image pre-generated using generative AI.

This game uses AI-assisted systems to support dynamic dialogue during interrogations with villagers. The AI helps generate variations in conversations to enhance immersion and replayability while maintaining the game’s narrative structure.
The game also uses AI-assisted systems to generate epilogues based on the player’s verdicts and the relationships between villagers. These epilogues help reflect the consequences of the player’s decisions and provide varied outcomes across playthroughs.
The dialogue and epilogue generation systems operate within structured prompts and developer-defined constraints to ensure consistency with the game’s design.
The AI systems are designed with safeguards to prevent inappropriate or harmful outputs. AI-assisted content is reviewed and refined during development to ensure it remains appropriate for the game’s setting and narrative.
Some visual assets were created with the assistance of generative AI tools. These assets were reviewed, edited, and refined by the developer before being implemented into the game.
All assets were checked to ensure they are appropriate and consistent with the game’s artistic direction.

1. Generative AI acts as your virtual Game Master: Classic lateral thinking puzzles rely on a human host's flexible judgment. We use AI to fulfill this role, instantly interpreting your open-ended questions in real-time to provide accurate "Yes," "No," or "Irrelevant" responses. This replaces rigid scripts with human-like judgment, allowing you to enjoy the full deduction experience solo.
2. AI empowers the Creation Mode: The AI can transform your simple prompts, scenarios, or endings into complete puzzle sets, allowing you to instantly generate fresh mysteries to play or share with others.
3. Visual assets are pre-generated by AI: To support the game's detective atmosphere, visual assets were generated with AI assistance, then carefully curated and integrated into the game.

This game uses AI-assisted tools for some pre-generated visual assets, textures, 3D models, UI/store artwork, marketing images, text, and code. Music and sound effects are not AI-generated.
During gameplay, AI-assisted procedural systems may generate runtime code-like logic and 3D model variations within predefined developer-controlled rules. The game does not use player-entered prompts, user uploads, or external AI services.

We integrated with Meshy to allow players to generate 3D furniture and decor for their rooms using a text prompt. Any 3D assets generated in this way are purely for personal use and cannot be placed on our download center.
Generative AI was not used in the making of our 2D artwork or included 3D assets.
Generative AI tools were used to assist in the creation of selected promotional and store artwork. During gameplay, players can also optionally use generative AI to create custom word sets and hints.

Penko Vox: Japanese uses local generative AI to power its immersive language learning experience. An integrated Large Language Model (LLM) acts as a native Japanese tutor, generating real-time dialogue based on user input, while a Neural Text-to-Speech (TTS) engine synthesizes high-fidelity Japanese audio for listening practice.

This game uses generative artificial intelligence technology to support the gameplay experience. Some character dialogue, case text, clue descriptions, hints, and interactive responses may be generated or assisted by AI in real time based on player input, case settings, and the current game state.
AI-generated content is constrained by game rules, story settings, content safety policies, and system limitations.

I created the ideas and basic writing for the in-game scenario, but chatGPT provided corrections, feedback, and translation assistance.
During the development process, AI-generated technology was used as an aid in the sketch and rough design stages. The generated elements were then finally adjusted and redrawn by the creator, to match the overall expressive style of the work.
